sketch.prompt:
1. Encapsulate components based on images when possible; 2. Use blob links for images; 3. Create a 1:1 replica of the image, refer to margins, sizes, fonts and backgrounds in the JSON array! 4. Use TypeScript; 5. For repeating elements in the image, use components when possible without breaking the original style; 6. Use text overflow styles, identify single/multi-line text, truncate with '...' for overflow to maintain aesthetics; 7. Use
tags, avoid

etc.; 8. Simplify CSS names, prefer flex layout over absolute positioning when possible; 9. Fix z-index issues where needed; 10. Maintain precise spacing as per reference data. Important: Don't omit any code!!!!

prompts.base: Please generate based on the uploaded design
prompts.react: React code using TypeScript and Tailwind CSS, project must have a start entry, and ensure the project can run, and ensure the code follows best practices and performance optimization.
prompts.vue: Vue3 code using TypeScript and Composition API, with Tailwind CSS styling, ensuring Vue best practices.
prompts.miniprogram: WeChat Mini Program code using the native framework with WXSS styling, following Mini Program development standards and best practices. Use rpx units for the interface, and remove the status bar if present in the design. Pay attention to styles and width when writing mini programs

welcome.title: Welcome to AppGen! Shall we look around?
welcome.body: A few seconds to find your bearings. Nothing to memorise — it all stays in sight.

chat.title: Describe what you want
chat.body: Write your idea in plain language: "an online shop with a cart and checkout". AppGen writes the code.

preview.title: The result, live
preview.body: Your application is built right here, in front of you. Switch between the code and the preview at any time.

header.title: Your settings
header.body: Model, language, theme and account: it all lives in this bar.

done.title: You are all set!
done.body: Make your first request. If the result is off, ask again differently — that is the point.

theme.title: Project theme
theme.subtitleBrand: Computed from the project's brand guidelines: contrast-verified palette, typography and rhythm.
theme.subtitleSeeded: Computed from a project-specific seed: no two projects get the same direction.
theme.applyPrompt: Apply this design system to the project (direction: {{direction}}). Follow the colors, typography and rhythm below.
theme.directionHint: What makes the page recognisable: surface, radii, section cadence.
theme.colorsHint: Ramps generated in OKLCH from the brand color.
theme.contrastHint: Measured, not estimated. WCAG AA for body text is 4.5:1.
theme.typographyHint: Display / body pairing, and the scale that follows from it.
theme.briefLabel: See the brief sent to the model
theme.error: The design system could not be computed.

versions.title: Version history
versions.hint: A restore point is saved on every generation.
versions.emptyBody: Your first generation will create a restore point.

chatWorkspace.startHint: Start the generation to get your application's code
chatWorkspace.inProgressBody: Your application is being generated. One moment…
chatWorkspace.completeBody: Your application is generated and ready to publish.

checks.title: Project checks
checks.subtitle: Two deterministic passes over the generated code. Neither calls a model: they are free and can be re-run at will.
checks.emptyBody: Checks run from the first generation onwards.
checks.error: The analysis could not complete. Try again shortly.

codeLoad.failedTitle: Your code could not be retrieved
codeLoad.failedBody: This project's code is saved, but fetching it failed. This is usually temporary.

help.title: Getting started with iCode
help.subtitle: Describe what you want, iCode writes the application. Here is what you can do next.

chat.title: Describe, then refine
chat.body: Write your request in plain language. Every exchange updates the code and saves a restore point, available from the ⋯ menu.

modes.title: Plan or Build
modes.body: Build edits the code. Plan never does: it reads your files and logs to answer "why is this failing" without rewriting anything.

toolbar.title: Edit from the preview
toolbar.body: The floating toolbar offers four tools: navigate, select an element to ask the AI about it, fix text by clicking into it (no credits used), or sketch the change you want.

theme.title: Theme and checks
theme.body: The Theme tab shows the palette computed for your project with measured contrast. The Checks tab flags design and security issues before you publish.

publish.title: Publish
publish.body: The Publish button puts your app online. The code stays standard React: download it or push it to GitHub from the ⋯ menu.
